label: Person
name: Adenis Roberto de Oliveira
summary:
Adenis Roberto de Oliveira is a Roman Catholic bishop in Brazil, serving the Church in one of the world's most Catholic nations and the largest country in Latin America. His ministry represents the post-Vatican II Brazilian Church, shaped by the legacy of the Medellín (1968) and Puebla (1979) conferences that reoriented Latin American Catholicism toward the poor and vulnerable.

Brazil's Catholic Church is remarkable for its size, diversity, and the theological creativity it has generated — liberation theology, the base ecclesial communities (CEBs), and the theology of inculturation all have deep Brazilian roots. At the same time, the Brazilian Church navigates a complex landscape of rapid Pentecostal growth, secularisation in urban areas, and the persistent social inequalities that demand prophetic witness.

De Oliveira's episcopal ministry contributes to the local Church's mission in his region of Brazil, implementing the priorities of a Church that Pope Francis has consistently held up as a model of pastoral dynamism. His service reflects the Brazilian Church's ongoing effort to maintain its massive institutional presence — in parishes, schools, hospitals, and social welfare organisations — while renewing its evangelical witness for a changing society.
